raw_segments.text: These virtues are of two sorts—natural and acquired.
By natural I mean not that which a man hath from his birth, for that is nothing else but
sense wherein men differ so little one from another and from brute beasts as it is not
But I mean that wit which is gotten by use only and experience without method, culture,
This natural wit consisteth principally in two things—cellarity of imagining—that
is swift succession of one thought to another and steady direction to some approved end.
On the contrary a slow imagination maketh that defect or fault of the mind which is
commonly called dullness, stupidity, and sometimes by other names that signify slowness of motion
